title: Color-Vision Deficiency Compensation: Reading Standard Vertical & Horizontal Signal Positions

no_head_on_same_lane.note: Oncoming vehicles on left are in separate lane divided by double-yellow; no head-on facing within same lane.

no_rhd_cabin.note: No car interiors or steering wheels visible; only exterior rear views.

single_bulb_signal.note: Both inset housings show three lit lenses at once: left vertical has top red, middle yellow, bottom green all illuminated; right horizontal has far-left red, middle yellow, far-right green all illuminated.

us_right_hand_traffic.note: Travel lane on right with white edge line/curb on far right; double-yellow centerline on left of travel lane with oncoming traffic left of it.

zero_text.note: No letters, numbers, or words visible; plates, sky and road are blank shapes.

scene_match.note: Image shows the requested left vertical and right horizontal signal housings against sky over highway, matching the described layout.

result.summary: Shows correct vertical/horizontal signal layouts but violates single-lit-lens rule by lighting all three lenses in both housings, teaching incorrect signal operation.

teaching_correct.note: Both housings illuminate all three lenses simultaneously, which never occurs in operation and defeats color-blind position learning.

result.what_i_see: Top insets show a vertical traffic signal on the left and horizontal signal on the right with all lenses lit, over a sunset multi-lane highway with cars driving away in the foreground.
